articles.title: GHSA: djust: Unsigned client state snapshot is restored as trusted view state (privilege escalation / state injection)
articles.summary:
### Impact
For views that opt into state snapshots, the snapshot `state_json` embedded in the client page was restored on reconnect as **trusted** view state with no integrity check. A client could edit the unsigned `state_json` in their page and return it in the reconnect mount frame to **inject arbitrary view attributes** — e.g. flip `is_admin` to `True`, or change `account_id` / `balance` — esc

articles.title: GHSA: djust: SSE sessions are not bound to the authenticated user; the client-chosen session_id is the sole authorization capability (session hijack)
articles.summary:
### Impact
SSE sessions were keyed solely by a **client-chosen** `session_id` with no binding to the authenticated user — a control the WebSocket transport has but that was dropped on SSE. An attacker who learns (or a victim who leaks) a `session_id` could connect to the message endpoint and dispatch event handlers that execute with the **victim's identity and state**.
